extracted_claims.text: As adopted in June 2024 (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), obligations for high-risk AI systems were to become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e., around 2 August 2026.

Under the originally adopted AI Act, Article 113(c) set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Chapter III, Sections 1-3 (the high-risk rules, including Annex III systems), with some narrower exceptions.

The Commission proposed in a 'Digital Omnibus on AI' / 'AI Omnibus' package to delay application of the high-risk Annex III rules by up to 16 months, tying the new start date to confirmation that needed standards and tools are available.
The AI Omnibus legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025.

Council and Parliament reached a political agreement on the AI Omnibus on 7 May 2026, which set new dates: 2 December 2027 for Annex III high-risk AI systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I (product-embedded) high-risk AI systems.
The AI Omnibus amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.
As a result of the Omnibus amendment, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027.

The obligations for high-risk AI systems that are classified as high-risk because they are safety components or products covered by Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) now apply from 2 August 2028.

The amended Regulation (consolidated EN version dated 27.07.2026) states that it applies to operators of certain already-placed/put-into-service high-risk AI systems only if those systems undergo significant design changes as from 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113', reflecting the new (Dec 2027) date rather than 2 August 2026.
A separate EU guidance page (Article 111 summary) still quotes the operator transition rule using the date '2 August 2026' rather than the revised Chapter III application date.
The Digital Omnibus on AI is formally identified as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, which sets 2 December 2027 for Article 6(2)/Annex III high-risk obligations.

Some commentary describes 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as 'backstop' dates that would apply automatically if the Omnibus amendments were not approved before 2 August 2026, implying uncertainty prior to formal adoption.

Several industry/legal-analysis sources (dated or apparently written before the Omnibus's entry into force) continue to state that the Annex III high-risk obligations become enforceable/applicable on 2 August 2026, without reference to the Omnibus delay.

Other obligations under the AI Act—such as prohibitions (from 2 February 2025, with certain deepfake/CSAM prohibitions from 2 December 2026), governance rules and GPAI obligations (from 2 August 2025), and Article 50 transparency obligations (generally from 2 August 2026, with a transitional deadline of 2 December 2026 for marking/detection under Article 50(2))—are distinct from, and unaffected by, the Annex III high-risk timeline change.

contradictions.claim_a: Annex III high-risk AI obligations apply from 2 August 2026, per the AI Act as adopted in 2024.
contradictions.claim_b: Annex III high-risk AI obligations now apply from 2 December 2027, following the AI Omnibus amendment that entered into force on 27 July 2026.
contradictions.description: Sources describing the originally adopted 2024 text (and several undated or pre-Omnibus commentary pieces) state 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III obligations, while sources reporting on the 2026 AI Omnibus amendment state the date has been moved to 2 December 2027. The discrepancy reflects a legislative change rather than a factual error, but sources that do not acknowledge the amendment present outdated information as current.

contradictions.claim_a: The EU AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 guidance page quotes the significant-design-change rule using the fixed date '2 August 2026'.
contradictions.claim_b: The consolidated, amended text of the Regulation (as of 27 July 2026) replaces the fixed 2 August 2026 reference with 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113', which is now 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems.
contradictions.description: Source 2 appears to reproduce a pre-Omnibus version of Article 111(2) still citing 2 August 2026, whereas source 1 is the post-Omnibus consolidated version referencing the (now later) Chapter III application date, indicating source 2 may be outdated or unupdated guidance.

contradictions.claim_a: The AI Omnibus delay to Annex III obligations was only a Commission proposal, with the new dates framed as conditional 'backstop' dates dependent on approval before 2 August 2026.
contradictions.claim_b: The AI Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) has been adopted, agreed politically (7 May 2026), and entered into force (27 July 2026), making 2 December 2027 a confirmed, binding date.
contradictions.description: Source 15 frames the 2027/2028 dates as contingent 'backstop' scenarios dependent on timely legislative approval, while source 16 and others describe the same dates as a 'confirmed, binding change' now in force, reflecting different points in the legislative timeline or differing certainty in characterization.

open_issues: The exact text and article numbering of the final AI Omnibus regulation (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) amending Article 6(2)/Annex III and Article 113 is not fully reproduced in the sources, so the precise legal mechanism and any conditional/carve-out provisions are unclear.

It is unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date is now an unconditional fixed date or whether it remains linked to confirmation of availability of harmonised standards and conformity assessment tools, as originally proposed by the Commission.

Several industry and legal-analysis sources have not been updated to reflect the Omnibus delay and still present 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline; it is unclear whether these reflect publication dates prior to 7 May/27 July 2026 or simple lack of updates.

The sources do not clarify whether any sub-categories of Annex III systems (e.g., those already placed on the market before 2 August 2026) face different compliance timelines or grandfathering rules beyond the general 'significant design change' trigger.

It is not fully explained how enforcement and market surveillance obligations (e.g., Article 50 transparency, GPAI governance) interact procedurally with the delayed Annex III timeline during the 2026–2027 transition period.
report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act, as adopted in June 2024, originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). However, following a 2026 "AI Omnibus" legislative amendment, this deadline has been pushed back: Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027**, while Annex I (product-embedded) high-risk systems have a separate deadline of **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (2024 Text)
As adopted in June 2024 (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), high-risk AI system obligations were set to apply 36 months after entry into force—around 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)). Article 113(c) of the originally adopted text specifically designated 2 August 2026 as the application date for Chapter III, Sections 1–3, covering the Annex III high-risk rules, with narrower exceptions (medium confidence) ([AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113); [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" package to delay the Annex III rules by up to 16 months, tying the new start date to confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools would be available (high confidence) ([Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). This proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025 (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026, confirming new dates: 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I systems (high confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Dates
As a result of the Omnibus amendment, Annex III high-risk AI system obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Obligations for high-risk systems classified under Annex I (safety components/products subject to Union harmonisation legislation) apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [LinkedIn - Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). The consolidated EUR-Lex text indicates that transitional rules for already-placed high-risk systems undergoing significant design changes are now tied to the revised Chapter III application date rather than the original 2 August 2026 date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

### Unaffected Obligations
Other AI Act obligations remain on their original schedule and are unaffected by the Annex III delay: prohibitions took effect 2 February 2025 (with deepfake/CSAM-related prohibitions from 2 December 2026), governance rules and GPAI obligations began 2 August 2025, and Article 50 transparency obligations generally apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act); [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Multiple industry and legal-analysis sources continue to state 2 August 2026 as the Annex III deadline without acknowledging the Omnibus amendment, likely reflecting pre-amendment publication dates (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)). Notably, the EU's own Article 111 guidance page still cites 2 August 2026, appearing inconsistent with the amended consolidated text (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

**Low-confidence claims flagged:** The formal identification of the Omnibus regulation as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" is sourced from only two lower-authority blogs (low confidence, 0.14) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)). Similarly, characterizations of the 2027/2028 dates as merely "backstop" dates contingent on timely approval—rather than confirmed—derive from a single social media source (low confidence, 0.12) ([LinkedIn - Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)), contradicting other sources describing the dates as settled.

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise legal text, article numbering, and any conditional provisions in the final Omnibus regulation remain unclear. It is uncertain whether the 2 December 2027 date is now unconditional or still linked to standards availability. Grandfathering rules for systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 are not fully specified, nor is the procedural interaction between the delayed Annex III timeline and unaffected obligations (e.g., Article 50, GPAI governance) during the transition period.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act, as adopted in June 2024, originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). However, following a 2026 "AI Omnibus" legislative amendment, this deadline has been pushed back: Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027**, while Annex I (product-embedded) high-risk systems have a separate deadline of **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (2024 Text)
As adopted in June 2024 (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), high-risk AI system obligations were set to apply 36 months after entry into force—around 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)). Article 113(c) of the originally adopted text specifically designated 2 August 2026 as the application date for Chapter III, Sections 1–3, covering the Annex III high-risk rules, with narrower exceptions (medium confidence) ([AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113); [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" package to delay the Annex III rules by up to 16 months, tying the new start date to confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools would be available (high confidence) ([Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). This proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025 (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026, confirming new dates: 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I systems (high confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Dates
As a result of the Omnibus amendment, Annex III high-risk AI system obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Obligations for high-risk systems classified under Annex I (safety components/products subject to Union harmonisation legislation) apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [LinkedIn - Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). The consolidated EUR-Lex text indicates that transitional rules for already-placed high-risk systems undergoing significant design changes are now tied to the revised Chapter III application date rather than the original 2 August 2026 date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

### Unaffected Obligations
Other AI Act obligations remain on their original schedule and are unaffected by the Annex III delay: prohibitions took effect 2 February 2025 (with deepfake/CSAM-related prohibitions from 2 December 2026), governance rules and GPAI obligations began 2 August 2025, and Article 50 transparency obligations generally apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act); [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Multiple industry and legal-analysis sources continue to state 2 August 2026 as the Annex III deadline without acknowledging the Omnibus amendment, likely reflecting pre-amendment publication dates (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)). Notably, the EU's own Article 111 guidance page still cites 2 August 2026, appearing inconsistent with the amended consolidated text (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

**Low-confidence claims flagged:** The formal identification of the Omnibus regulation as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" is sourced from only two lower-authority blogs (low confidence, 0.14) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)). Similarly, characterizations of the 2027/2028 dates as merely "backstop" dates contingent on timely approval—rather than confirmed—derive from a single social media source (low confidence, 0.12) ([LinkedIn - Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)), contradicting other sources describing the dates as settled.

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise legal text, article numbering, and any conditional provisions in the final Omnibus regulation remain unclear. It is uncertain whether the 2 December 2027 date is now unconditional or still linked to standards availability. Grandfathering rules for systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 are not fully specified, nor is the procedural interaction between the delayed Annex III timeline and unaffected obligations (e.g., Article 50, GPAI governance) during the transition period.
